title: Retentive part counter
summary: A part counter must keep the shift count when the PLC makes a warm restart, but a cold restart starts a new shift at zero. Make the right variable retentive.
objectives: Declare a retentive variable with VAR RETAIN
Predict what a warm and a cold restart do to retentive and non-retentive data
Verify retention with the online variable detail and the diagnostic buffer
instructions: Build and load the program, set the PLC to RUN and let the proximity sensor see a few parts.
In Advanced mode, make a warm restart. Watch Count in the online variable detail: with the starter program it starts again from 0.
Move Count into a VAR RETAIN section, load again and repeat: the count must survive the warm restart.
Make a cold restart and check that the count starts again from its initial value. Then run Check.
hints: A warm restart keeps only variables declared in VAR RETAIN; everything else returns to its initial value.
Function block instances such as R_TRIG are not retentive in PLC Lab. Retain the counted value, not the block.

scenarios.title: Parts, a warm restart, one more part, a cold restart

criteria.title: Two parts are counted
criteria.onFail: Count was not 2 after two parts. Count one part per rising edge of PartPresent.

criteria.title: The count survives a warm restart
criteria.onFail: After the warm restart and one more part Count was not 3: the count was not kept. Declare it in VAR RETAIN.

criteria.title: Lamp H1 shows three parts
criteria.onFail: Lamp1 was off with three parts counted.

criteria.title: A cold restart starts a new shift
criteria.onFail: After the cold restart Count was not back to its initial value 0.
